title: Four in ten
hook: In 1900 four in ten children died before turning five. How fast did that change?

knows: many children died in the past
doesNotKnow: that the figure barely moved through the 1800s
that most of the fall came after 1950

misconception: Child deaths fell slowly and steadily over the last few centuries.
objective: The learner can say that Gapminder's world estimate of children dying before 5 barely moved from 1800 (430 per 1,000) to 1900 (411), then fell to 37 by 2020, about 11 times fewer, with more than half of that fall after 1950.

claims.text: Gapminder's world estimate of children dying before age 5 per 1,000 born, each year from 1800 to 2020: 430 in 1800, 411 in 1900, 246 in 1950, 37 in 2020.
claims.source: history-data.mjs: gmu5, gapminder-u5mr-global.csv, column child_mortality_0_5_year_olds_dying_per_1000_born (concept u5mr, 'the probability of dying between birth and exactly five years of age', ddf--concepts.csv, opened by cm-history). The 221 values for 1800-2020 are copied into Demo.tsx unchanged; history-cycle2-check.mjs section 13 '13 1900 and 2020'.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Re-derived in my own node script from the pinned file (history-data.mjs pins all hold; sha256 re-checked) and compared with the copied array in Demo.tsx (identical). 221 values 1800-2020: 1800 430, 1900 411, 1950 246, 2020 37. Concept (ddf--concepts.csv, opened): u5mr v12, 'the probability of dying between birth and exactly five years of age expressed per 1000 live births'.

claims.text: From 1900 to 2020 the figure fell about 11 times (411 to 37).
claims.source: 411 / 37 = 11.1, rounded to 11. Computed in Demo.tsx; history-cycle2-check.mjs section 13.

claims.text: In the century before 1900 the figure barely moved, from 430.
claims.source: 1800 430 to 1900 411: 19 fewer per 1,000 in a century. history-cycle2-check.mjs section 13 '13 flat before 1900'.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): 1800 430 to 1900 411. In between the series reaches 444 (max 1800-1900), so 'barely moved' is fair: it stayed within 411-444 for a century.

claims.text: More than half of the fall since 1900, 56%, came after 1950.
claims.source: (246 - 37) / (411 - 37) = 0.559, shown as 56%. history-cycle2-check.mjs section 13 '13 share of the fall after 1950'.
411 / 10 and 37 / 10, rounded. history-cycle2-check.mjs section 13 '13 out of 100'.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): 41.1 and 3.7 per 100, rounded 41 and 4.

claims.text: Where it stops: this is one source's world figure, and some of its early values are guesses or modelled, not counted.
claims.source: OWID grapher metadata for child-mortality (ourworldindata.org/grapher/child-mortality.metadata.json, descriptionProcessing, opened by FC41): OWID drops Gapminder rows labelled 'Guesstimate' or 'Model based on Life Expectancy'. 'One source's world figure' follows from the file being a single Gapminder world aggregate (history-data.mjs: gmu5).
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Held. Not verified on trust. Fix (builder): use the named fallback, 'Where it stops: this is one source's world figure, an average over very different places.' That follows from the file being a single world aggregate. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): UNVERIFIED. HELD. Gapminder's u5mr documentation is still unreachable: gapminder.org is on the allow-list but redirects to www.gapminder.org, which the proxy blocks (403), and gapm.io fails. Opened instead: OWID grapher metadata for child-mortality (ourworldindata.org/grapher/child-mortality.metadata.json), OWID 'Mortality in the past' and 'Child and infant mortality' articles. None says that record coverage thins as the series goes back. They say Gapminder 'provides estimates of child mortality rates from 1800 to 2015', that OWID drops Gapminder rows labelled 'Guesstimate' or 'Model based on Life Expectancy', and that Sweden's Tabellverket (1749) was the first office for population statistics. That is suggestive, not the claim. Fix (history-builder), checkable now: 'Where it stops: this is one source's world figure, and some of its early values are guesses or modelled, not counted.' (source: OWID child-mortality metadata, descriptionProcessing). Or the pass-39 fallback ('an average over very different places'). | v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-15): FC41 c6 fix: wording now the one FC41 named as checkable from the OWID metadata; was 'the further back it goes, the fewer places kept records to build it from'. Reset to unverified for a fact-checker who is not the builder. | FC pass 43 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Reveal: 'Where it stops: this is one source's world figure, and some of its early values are guesses or modelled, not counted.' Inference noted: OWID describes Gapminder's country data (v7), and the world figure is built from it; the pinned 1800-1851 world values sit at 423-430 with multi-year flat runs, which is what modelled values look like. I found no Gapminder page reachable that labels the world aggregate's years directly.

claims.text: In 1900 four in ten children died before turning five (hook).
claims.source: 411 per 1,000 = 41 in 100, about four in ten (c1, c5).

recall.question: Child deaths in a town fall from 300 to 30 per 1,000 born. How does the number of children reaching age 5 change?
recall.why: Survivors go from 700 to 970 per 1,000, about 40% more: a tenfold fall in deaths is not a tenfold rise in survivors.
